findings.description: The inline policy grants wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", giving the deploy user unrestricted control of compute, storage and serverless resources account-wide. ec2:* and lambda:* combined with iam:PassRole-dependent workflows create a privilege-escalation path, and s3:* allows reading or deleting any bucket data.

A permanent IAM access key is minted for a near-admin user and, with no pgp_key set, the plaintext secret is persisted in Terraform state. Static non-rotating keys for a highly privileged identity should be replaced with short-lived STS role credentials.
A long-lived IAM user holding account-wide wildcard permissions is created with no permissions_boundary and no MFA-conditioned access, so there is no containment if its credentials leak.

The output exposes IAM access key material without sensitive = true, so it can be rendered in plan/apply console output and CI logs and retrieved with terraform output. Note that because no pgp_key is configured on the access key, encrypted_secret will be empty, but the output is still an unsafe pattern for credential material.
